title: Tech Lead
description: WeFlex exists to increase the life expectancy and quality of life for people with a disability, people in aged care, and Australian war veterans — through access to physical fitness, allied health, and therapy supports. We've delivered over 50,000 sessions of support across our network, grown 30x over the last 2.5 years, and want to continue at a rate of 100% year on year. The seat You'll own the technology engine that powers WeFlex's end-to-end customer lifecycle — lead acquisition through retention. Today it runs across Supabase, Airtable, n8n, GoHighLevel, Zendesk, Aircall, Wavix, Xero, and our internal portals. Tomorrow it's your call to architect. You sit at the leadership table as a senior peer — reporting to our COO, partnering directly with the CEO, working alongside our Heads of Sales, CS, Marketing, and (soon) Service Providers. This is a player-coach seat. You don't just architect — you build. Then you lead a team of 5 builders to ship alongside you. Big problems we're chewing on right now: the O2C rebuild (kill Zoho), the Supabase migration (centralise source-of-truth), the AHP supervision automation that's worth ~$185k/yr in revenue if we get it right. AI augmentation is non-negotiable. We move at a pace where the only way to keep up is to have Claude / GPT / Cursor / equivalents deeply embedded in how you think and ship every day. If they're not already core to your workflow, this role isn't for you. The 5 things you'll do day-to-day: Set the technology strategy — what we build, what we migrate, what we kill. The 18-month roadmap is yours to author with the COO + CEO. Architect + build — you write the spec, then you ship the work. We don't promote you out of code. The team builds with you, not for you. Lead and grow the team — hire, performance manage, build capability, exit underperformers when needed. We have 5 builders today; you'll shape the next 10. Partner directly with CEO + COO — translate ambiguous business problems into systems that work. "Clients aren't reporting back" ? you diagnose, scope, ship. AI-augmented by default — Claude, GPT, Cursor, equivalent are part of how you ship every day, not just how you write email s. Show us your stack and a real recent build where AI was core to how you executed. What we're looking for We hire skills over credentials. AI-augmented operator (non-negotiable). Your workflow runs through Claude / GPT / Cursor — diagnosing, scoping, building, documenting. If AI is bolted on rather than core, this role won't work. Builder of systems with real artifacts. Operational systems / integrations / automations you've shipped end-to-end. Portfolio over CV. Show us the code, the flows, the Looms. Architectural judgment at scale. You've made build-vs-buy / migrate-vs-rebuild calls. You've owned a platform decision and can defend it. You think in trade-offs, not absolutes. Track record leading a small tech team. Hiring, performance management, capability building, hard conversations. We have 5 builders; you'll d ---------- who stays, who grows, who goes. Translates ambiguous executive briefs into shipped systems. When the CEO says "we need to know which clients are at risk" — you diagnose, scope, build, ship. You don't wait for the perfect spec. Degree, years-of-experience, prior industry — all signals, not gates. If your work speaks, your CV doesn't have to be conventional. What this role does NOT involve ? Marketing tech / GHL funnel design ? marketing team owns this ? Direct customer service ? CS team owns Zendesk as a product ? Heavy DevOps / infrastructure architecture ? we're a small remote team running on managed services ? Mobile / native app development ? we run web + portal stack Compensation PHP 90,000–220,000 per month depending on experience and demonstrated capability Fully remote, AEST-aligned working hours Career trajectory: This is the technology counterpart to our COO-track seat. For the right person, ownership expands as we scale — through Head of Engineering and beyond — as WeFlex grows. To apply Submit your application here: ---------- The application has two parts: Part 1 — Application form Your CV Portfolio link (GitHub, Loom library, case studies, live systems you've built) 3 short written answers Notice period + salary expectation Part 2 — Build task A real WeFlex scenario with sample data. You build a working artifact and record a short Loom walking us through your thinking, your tool choice, and your AI workflow. No time limit — we score the quality of the build, not how fast you finished. Full briefing pack is provided when you start the application. We hire builders, not talkers. The build task is the highest-weight signal in our process.

description: Project Overview I am looking for an experienced automation/API developer to build Phase 1 of a field service intake automation system. This project involves CallTrackingMetrics, FieldPulse, n8n, webhooks, APIs, customer lookup, job creation, alerts, and AI voice intake. The goal of Phase 1 is not full dispatch or scheduling. The goal is to create a reliable intake system that captures qualified service requests, creates or updates the correct customer/job record, and sends alerts so a human can review and take over. Phase 1 Scope The first build should include these modules: Module 1 — Intake / Webhook Receiver Receive incoming call/contact/intake data through webhook or API. This may come from CallTrackingMetrics, an AI voice agent, web form, chatbot, or test payload. The workflow should capture and structure fields such as: Customer name Phone number Service location / city / ZIP Vehicle or equipment description Service issue Urgency Roadside / safety status if applicable Lead source / tracking number if available Call summary or transcript if available Module 2 — AI Voice Intake Assistant Set up or integrate an AI voice intake assistant that collects required intake information. The voice agent must act only as an intake assistant. It should not diagnose, estimate, schedule, dispatch, or promise response times. The voice agent should identify whether the caller is a qualified service request, out of area, sales/spam, existing customer follow-up, or needs human follow-up. Module 3 — FieldPulse Customer / Job Record Creation Use FieldPulse API or approved integration method to: Search for an existing customer before creating a new one Avoid duplicate customer records when possible Create or update customer information Create a job, lead, or service request record Attach relevant intake details, notes, call summary, source, and urgency Module 4 — Alerts and Human Review Output Send alerts when a qualified service request is received. Minimum alert output should include: Customer name Phone number City / ZIP / location Vehicle or equipment Service issue Urgency Roadside / safety status FieldPulse customer/job link if available Intake summary Whether the record was created, updated, or flagged for review Alerts may be sent by SMS, email , FieldPulse notification, or another agreed method. Important Rules This is Phase 1 only. The system should not automatically dispatch technicians, schedule appointments, give price estimates, diagnose mechanical problems, order parts, or promise arrival times. Human review remains part of the process. Required Experience Please apply only if you have experience with some or all of the following: n8n workflow automation Webhooks and REST APIs CRM or field-service software API integrations Customer lookup before creating new records Job, lead, or service request creation through API CallTrackingMetrics, FieldPulse, or similar platforms AI voice agents such as Vapi, Retell, Twilio, Bland, or similar Error handling, logging, and workflow documentation Preferred First Step I would like to start with a small fixed-price test module before the full build. The test module should prove that you can receive a sample intake payload, apply qualification logic, check for an existing customer, prepare a FieldPulse-ready record, and send a structured alert. Please include in your response: Relevant n8n/API/webhook projects you have built Whether you have worked with FieldPulse, CallTrackingMetrics, or similar platforms Whether you have built AI voice intake agents Your recommended approach for Phase 1 Estimated hours and cost for the first test module

That said, the expected monthly range is USD $500–$1,000(for full-time workers), depending on factors such as proficiency, workload, task complexity, performance (including bonuses), experience, skill set, and the final scope of responsibilities. [What You’ll Be Doing] Your role is to be the technical guardian and engine of our WordPress website. You will be responsible for all back-end aspects of the site, ensuring it is secure, fast, and scalable. Your main tasks will include: a) Custom Plugin & Theme Development: You will extend our website's functionality by developing custom plugins and theme features. This requires writing clean, well-documented code that adheres strictly to WordPress coding standards to ensure long-term maintainability and compatibility. b) Database Management & Optimization: You will be responsible for the health of our WordPress database. This includes writing efficient database queries to ensure fast page loads and implementing robust security and backup protocols to protect our data. c) Server-Side Scripting & PHP Logic: You will build and manage the core logic that powers our website's dynamic features. A deep understanding of PHP and WordPress Hooks (Actions and Filters) is essential to customize functionality without compromising the core structure. d) API Integration & Management: You will connect our website with third-party services and applications. This involves leveraging the WordPress REST API and ensuring all data exchange is handled securely and efficiently. e) Proactive Security & Maintenance: You will own our website's security posture. This involves implementing proactive security measures against common vulnerabilities (like XSS), performing regular malware scans, and diligently managing all updates for the WordPress core, themes, and plugins. f) Website Performance Optimization: You will be tasked with making our website as fast as possible. Your responsibilities will include implementing effective caching strategies, optimizing database queries, and minifying code and resources to improve user experience and SEO rankings. g) Advanced Troubleshooting & Debugging: When technical issues arise, you will be the expert responsible for diagnosing and resolving them. You must have strong problem-solving skills and be proficient with debugging tools to efficiently identify the root cause of any plugin conflict or server error. [Goal] The ultimate goal is to provide our business with a rock-solid, secure, and high-performing website. By transforming technical requirements into robust back-end solutions, you will ensure our digital platform is reliable, scalable, and provides a seamless experience for our users. You will be the engine of stability for our entire online operation. [What We’re Looking For] The ideal candidate: a) Has Verifiable WordPress Development Experience: You have a strong portfolio showcasing custom plugins, themes, or complex back-end solutions you have built for WordPress. b) Is a Master Problem-Solver: You can connect disparate symptoms to identify the root cause of a technical issue and can architect elegant, long-term solutions. c) Is Meticulous and Security-Focused: You have a passion for writing clean, efficient code and a methodical approach to website security and maintenance. d) Has a Proactive and Ownership Mindset: You don’t just fix problems as they appear; you anticipate future needs and continuously work to improve the website's performance and security. e) Is Proficient with the Modern WordPress Stack: You are highly skilled in PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, and the WordPress REST API, and are comfortable using modern development and debugging tools. f) Communicates with Clarity and Values Respect: You are reliable, accountable, and can explain complex technical issues in a clear, logical manner. *Important Note: We value respectful communication. What does it mean? Most importantly, if you need to step away, just let me or your manager know why and when. We understand it, even if you need to leave tomorrow, BUT ghosting is the last thing you'd like to do, since it causes confusion and delays. In everyday conversations, our team thrives on mutual respect, no matter your role. [Why Work With Us?] -Flexible hours to suit your lifestyle. -The opportunity to be the foundational technical owner of a growing digital platform. -Long-term growth opportunities as our company scales. -A supportive environment where your technical expertise is valued and your impact is visible. [About Us] We are a growing team dedicated to providing an exceptional online experience in our industry. Our mission is to build a digital platform our audience can rely on. Your role is absolutely essential in building and maintaining the technical integrity that will make that mission a reality. [How to Apply] Subject Line: Start your title with either "Back-End WordPress Pro", or your application can't be considered. In your application, include: 1) Portfolio & Code Samples: Share your resume, links to just your best 1~2 works(preferably your previous client's websites, stating your specific role). Do not share a link to everything you've done. Time is very limited. 2) Imagine this: It's Monday morning, and you get an urgent message. A client's website is intermittently showing a blank white screen (the WordPress White Screen of Death). They say they haven't changed anything. You have FTP and database access. Tell me the first five steps you would take, in the exact order you would take them, and narrate your reasoning for each action. 3) Troubleshooting Challenge: Your client's WordPress site has suddenly become very slow. Describe your process for diagnosing the issue. What are the first five things you would investigate and why? 4) Security Challenge: You suspect a WordPress site has been compromised. Briefly outline the key steps you would take to identify the breach, clean the site, and harden it against future attacks. 5) Beyond the obvious answers, what is one specific part of the WordPress core API or architecture that you genuinely admire for its design, and why? Conversely, what is one part that you find consistently frustrating or poorly designed, and how do you typically work around its limitations in your projects? 6) Preferred Tool Stack: What is your go-to development environment? Please list any specific debugging tools, IDEs, and version control systems you prefer to use. 7) Explain where and how you use AI to improve your productivity, and where you deliberately choose not to rely on AI. (Wish you aren't using AI for answering these questions, because they will be further discussed in the interview later.) 8) Available Hours: Let us know your general availability (e.g., "Approximately 20 hours per week, mostly flexible between 1PM - 8PM on Monday, 3 PM - 10PM on Tuesday, 12PM - 8PM on Wednesday, ...,  in Philippines time"). 9) Available Period of Work: Let us know for how long you expect to work with us. Monthly SEO and website improvement plan (per clinic)

Google Business Profiles managed and tracked

We are building long-term systems, not short-term campaigns.

Systems & Optimization

title: WordPress Developer — Reverse Proxy Blog Migration
job_title: WordPress Developer — Reverse Proxy Blog Migration
description: WordPress Developer — Reverse Proxy Blog Migration Squarespace to WordPress on WP Engine Overview We need an experienced WordPress developer to migrate a blog (~850 pages) from Squarespace to WordPress on WP Engine. The main website stays on Squarespace — only the blog moves. A Cloudflare Worker reverse proxy will route blog traffic (/blog/*) to WordPress while all other traffic continues to Squarespace. All existing blog URLs must remain identical after migration. This is not a standard WordPress build. The reverse proxy routing is the core technical challenge. Scope of Work 1. WP Engine Setup. Provision WordPress environment, configure theme, install required plugins. Set up permalink structure to match existing blog URLs exactly. The site has two URL patterns: flat slugs (/blog/post-slug) and date-based paths (/blog/2024/10/19/post-slug). Both must resolve correctly. 2. Content Migration. Export content from Squarespace (WXR format), import into WordPress. Write and run scripts to download all images from Squarespace’s CDN, upload to WordPress media library, and rewrite all image URLs in post content. Verify all 850+ post slugs match the originals. 3. Cloudflare Worker & DNS. Move domain nameservers to Cloudflare. Write and deploy a Cloudflare Worker that routes /blog/* requests to WP Engine and passes all other requests through to Squarespace. Configure proper Host headers, X-Forwarded-Proto, and SSL end-to-end. 4. WordPress Proxy Configuration. Configure ---------- p for reverse proxy operation (WP_HOME, WP_SITEURL, forwarded headers). Ensure WordPress generates correct URLs through the proxy. No redirect loops, no mixed content. 5. URL Verification & QA. Verify every migrated URL returns HTTP 200 through the proxy. Test for redirect loops, broken images, mixed content warnings, and correct canonical URLs. Deliver a QA report covering all pages. Required Experience •  Cloudflare Workers — you’ve written and deployed them before, not just used Cloudflare for DNS •  Reverse proxy configuration — routing subdirectory traffic to a different origin server •  WP Engine hosting — familiar with their portal, domain config, caching, and SFTP/SSH access •  WordPress ---------- p for proxy setups — forwarded headers, WP_HOME vs WP_SITEURL •  Large-scale content migration — 850+ pages including scripted image re-hosting •  SSL/HTTPS configuration across proxied setups •  WP-CLI proficiency Project Details Budget: $1,500–$2,500 fixed price (open to discussion based on experience) Timeline: 3–4 weeks Type: Contract / project-based, with potential for ongoing WordPress maintenance Communication: Async via Slack or email . Weekly progress updates. You’ll work directly with our SEO lead who will provide technical direction and review work at each phase. To Apply Please include: 1. A specific example of a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Worker project you’ve completed. Describe the setup, not just “I’ve done it.” 2. A specific example of a large content migration (100+ pages), ideally Squarespace to WordPress. 3. Your availability to start and estimated completion timeline. 4. Your fixed-price quote for the full scope described above.

title: WooCommerce Developer (Full-Time, Remote)
description: # Job Posting: WooCommerce Developer (Full-Time, Remote) --- ## Job Title **WooCommerce Developer — Full-Time Remote (Long-Term)** --- ## Salary ?50,000 – ?60,000/month (based on experience and skills) --- ## Job Description We're looking for a **sharp, independent WooCommerce developer** to join our growing e-commerce brands full-time. This is not a one-time gig — we're building something long-term and need someone who thinks like a partner, not just a coder. You'll be the go-to developer for our WooCommerce stores. That means you own the technical side: building, optimizing, troubleshooting, and improving. You'll work directly with the founder — who thinks in outcomes and visuals, not code. That means **clear communication is just as important as clean code.** --- ## What You'll Do - Build and maintain WooCommerce stores from scratch (theme setup, plugin configuration, checkout optimization) - Customize themes and page builders (Elementor, or similar) so the team can update content without developer help - Integrate payment gateways, shipping plugins, and third-party tools (CRM, email marketing, supplier APIs) - Optimize site speed, mobile responsiveness, and SEO basics - Troubleshoot and fix issues quickly — without being asked twice - Proactively suggest improvements when you see something that could work better --- ## What We're Looking For ### Must-Have - **3+ years of hands-on WooCommerce experience** (not just WordPress — we need WooCommerce depth) - Strong knowledge of **PHP, HTML, CSS, JavaScript** - Experience with **Elementor** or other page builders - Experience setting up **payment gateways, shipping, and product variations** - Fluent English — written and spoken - Reliable internet and a proper work setup ### What Sets You Apart - You **ask questions** when a brief is unclear instead of guessing - You communicate with **screenshots, Loom videos, or staging links** — not just "it's done" - You've built stores that are **live and generating revenue** (share links, we'll check them) - You understand **site speed optimization** (you know what a 90+ PageSpeed score looks like) - You've worked with **dropshipping setups** (supplier integrations, auto-fulfillment, inventory sync) - You can explain technical decisions in **simple language** a non-developer understands --- ## How We Work - **Communication:** Daily async updates. We use chat (Slack/WhatsApp) + weekly video calls - **Tools:** Git for version control, staging environments before going live - **Mindset:** We value initiative. If you see a problem, flag it. If you have a better idea, share it. "Yes sir" without thinking is not what we need. - **Hours:** Full-time (40 hrs/week), flexible schedule with overlap in European timezone (CET) for calls --- ## To Apply — Read This Carefully **Do NOT send a generic "I am a WordPress expert" message.** Applications that don't follow these steps will be ignored. ### Step 1: Subject Line Use this exact subject line: **"WooCom Builder — [Your Name]"** ### Step 2: Portfolio Share **3 live WooCommerce stores** you built or significantly contributed to. For each one, tell us: - What was your role? - What was the biggest technical challenge? - What's the current PageSpeed score? (Google PageSpeed Insights — check it now) ### Step 3: Mini Test Look at this scenario and tell us how you'd approach it: > *"We're launching a new dropshipping store. The supplier provides a product feed via CSV that updates daily. We need products to auto-sync (price, stock, images) into WooCommerce without manual work. The store needs to look premium, load fast on mobile, and have a smooth checkout. What's your approach? What tools/plugins would you use? What questions would you ask before starting?"* Write your answer in **max 200 words.** We're looking for clarity, not length. ### Step 4: Availability - When can you start? - What are your working hours? - Do you have other ongoing clients? (Honesty is valued — we just need to know) --- ## Why This Role - **Above-market salary** with room to grow as we scale - **Long-term position** — not a revolving door of freelance gigs - **Direct access to the founder** — no middle management, no bureaucracy - **Real impact** — you're not maintaining someone else's mess, you're building from the ground up - **Growth potential** — as we add more stores, your role (and compensation) grows with us --- *We review applications within 5 business days. If we like what we see, we'll start with a small paid test project before committing to the full role.*

# Intermediate WordPress Developer (Execution-Focused, Debugging-Heavy)

## About The Role
We’re looking for an intermediate WordPress developer who knows how to **figure things out, fix issues, and get things working reliably**.
This is not a “build pretty sites from scratch” role.
This is a **high-impact execution role** focused on:
- debugging real-world issues
- maintaining and improving live websites
- implementing designs accurately
- optimizing performance

If you enjoy solving problems like *“Why is this form not submitting?”* or *“Why is this site slow?”* - you’ll thrive here.

---

## What You’ll Be Doing
This role is roughly:
- **80% support, debugging, and fixes**
- **20% optimization and improvements**

### Core Responsibilities
- Diagnose and fix issues across WordPress sites (forms, plugins, themes, integrations)
- Maintain and support existing client websites
- Implement designs with high attention to detail using:
-- builders (Avada, Beaver Builder, etc.)
-- custom templates (ACF-based)
- Perform performance optimization (Core Web Vitals, load speed improvements)
- Handle API integrations (forms, CRMs, third-party tools)
- Execute SEO-related technical implementations
- Collaborate with teammates on QA (your own work and teammates’ work)

---

## What Success Looks Like
- You can take a vague issue like *“something is broken”* and figure out the root cause
- You **ask the right questions**, scope the solution, and execute it cleanly
- You can independently fix performance issues across the stack (DNS ? server ? WordPress)
- Your work is thoughtful
- You consistently deliver

---

## Required Skills & Experience

### WordPress Fundamentals
- Strong understanding of how WordPress works:
- themes, plugins, templates
- Experience with:
- **ACF (Advanced Custom Fields)** for custom templates
- Gutenberg vs builder-based themes (and when to use each)

### Frontend Development
- Strong CSS skills (must be able to implement designs accurately)
- Solid JavaScript (understanding of jQuery + modern JS is required, but proficiency is not required)
- Ability to translate designs into functional WP layouts

### Backend / Systems Awareness
- Working knowledge of PHP within WordPress
- Understanding of the **LAMP stack**
- Ability to troubleshoot performance and uptime issues:
- hosting, DNS, caching, plugins, etc.

### Debugging & Problem Solving (Critical)
- Ability to diagnose issues independently
- Comfortable working with incomplete information
- Able to propose solutions

---

## How You’ll Work
- Fully remote, globally distributed team
- Work directly with our project managers and other developers
- Minimal meetings (a few per week), but **must be available for real-time collaboration in 8am-5pm CST timezone**

### Schedule (Non-Negotiable)
- Must work within **8am–5pm CST**
- Typical expectation:
- ~4 hours per weekday (e.g., 9am–1pm CST M-F)

---

## Compensation
- Commensurate with experience
- Guaranteed and consistent weekday hours
- Opportunity to grow into:
- full-time role
- senior developer positions

---

## What Makes This Role Different
- High autonomy, no micromanagement
- Real-world problem solving (not repetitive production work)
- Exposure to:
- Senior WordPress developer teammates with vast experiences
- performance optimization
- SEO implementation
- complex debugging scenarios
- Fast-paced environment with a variety of projects

---

## What We’re Looking For (Soft Skills)
- Strong written and spoken English (required)
- Clear, proactive communication
- Ability to ask smart questions and move things forward
- Detail-oriented - especially with design implementation

---

## Who This Is NOT For
- Developers who only rely on plugins without understanding how things work
- Pure designers with limited technical depth

---

## Growth Opportunity
This role is designed as a stepping stone to:
- Senior WordPress Developer
- Technical specialist (performance, SEO, systems)
- Expanded responsibility across projects and architecture

---

If you’re the type of developer who enjoys solving problems, improving systems, and making things work under real-world conditions, we’d love to hear from you!

---

The Mighty Mo! is a seasoned WordPress development, design, and SEO agency based in Minneapolis, MN, focused on delivering high-quality results you'll be proud of.

Here’s why our team loves working here:
- Regular Hours
- Asynchronous + Real Time Communication – Minimal meetings; we use ClickUp to stay organized.

description: Rate: $14–18/hr (starting), with raise to $18/hr at 90 days based on performance Hours: 10 hrs/week (~43 hrs/month), mostly async with 1-hour weekly sync call Company: Pharmacy Pearls LLC — US-based pharmacy education company. We run a live LMS serving hundreds of pharmacists preparing for board exams (BCEMP, BCCCP, BCPS), an AI-powered medical research platform, and an AI podcast pipeline. --- Why this role exists We have two excellent full-stack developers who ship production features with Claude Code every day. They do great work — but no one is critically reviewing their code. We need a senior developer who will block bad PRs, catch architectural mistakes, and mentor the team. This is NOT a feature-coding role. You will review their work, propose architectural improvements, and make sure our platform doesn't collect tech debt or security holes. Think of it as the role a staff engineer or tech lead plays — but focused on review and advisory, not building. --- What you'll do (10 hrs/week) - Review 4–8 pull requests per week with actual line-level comments (not "LGTM") - Block PRs that aren't ready — enforce testing, security, and code-quality standards - 1-hour weekly sync call with the founder + 2 developers (Manila morning, your 8–10 AM) - Async architecture input on design docs before devs start coding - Monthly 1-page codebase health report (tech debt, risks, recommendations) - Answer ad-hoc async questions about security, DB design, auth patterns What you will NOT do - Write feature code (our devs handle that) - Own delivery timelines or sprint planning - Handle client communication or support --- Required skills - 8+ years full-stack JavaScript/TypeScript - React / Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL (production experience, not tutorials) - Daily Claude Code user — you must use Claude Code yourself. We'll ask to see your setup. - Code review experience — you have reviewed other developers' PRs and left line-level comments - Written English at C1/C2 level — your review comments must be clear and professional - Willingness to push back respectfully — if the founder proposes something bad, you say so Strongly preferred - AI/LLM integration experience (Claude API, RAG pipelines, vector databases) - Drizzle or Prisma ORM - Supabase, pgvector - Observability tools (BetterStack, Sentry, Datadog) - Testing discipline (Vitest, Jest, integration tests with real DBs) - Security mindset (OWASP familiarity, auth/session patterns) --- Our stack TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM, Supabase, pgvector, Tailwind CSS, BetterStack, Stripe, ClickUp, WordPress (legacy), Claude API, Voyage AI, OpenAI, Cartesia TTS --- How to apply To be considered, include ALL of the following in your application. Applications missing any item will be skipped. 1. Your Claude Code workflow — screenshot of your CLAUDE.md file or a ~/.claude/ directory listing. When do you use Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku? What slash commands or skills have you created? 2. A link to one pull request you reviewed where you left at least 5 line-level comments that were not just approvals. If the repo is private, share a redacted screenshot. 3. Answer this in 200 words or less: "A junior developer on the team opens a 170-file pull request that mixes three unrelated features — a dashboard, a notification system, and a database migration. All tests pass. The founder wants it shipped this week. What do you do?" 4. Your rate preference between $10/hr and $14/hr, and why you'd accept a part-time retainer vs. a full-time gig. 5. Years of React/Node/TypeScript/PostgreSQL experience — specific numbers per stack. --- Red flags that will get your application skipped - Generic "I am hardworking and detail-oriented" cover letters - No Claude Code evidence - "LGTM" as your concept of a real code review - Inflated experience claims (listing "5 years React" with a LinkedIn showing you started it last year) - Asking to write feature code "to help" --- What to expect if shortlisted - 30-minute video interview (we will ask you to share your screen and show Claude Code in action) - Paid 1-hour code review trial ($20) — you review a real PR from our codebase and leave written comments - If the trial goes well, we start immediately with a 2-week probation period Response time: We reply to all qualified applicants within 3 business days. We typically receive 100+ applications within 48 hours, so please make yours specific. Looking forward to meeting you.

Solid working knowledge of **PHP** in the context of WordPress development. - Experience building and customising sites with **WordPress**, including theme and plugin development. - Proficiency with **Elementor** page builder for layout creation and management, using Hello Elementor as a theme base. - Willingness to receive and make phone calls to assist customers directly. - Willingness to sign an NDA and Non-Compete Agreement. ## Nice to Have - Experience with **Cloudflare** — particularly security configuration, DNS management, and Cloudflare Stream. - Familiarity with caching strategies (object caching, CDN configuration, page caching plugins). - Experience with site migration and DNS management. ## What We Value - A problem-solving mindset — you're resourceful and enjoy figuring things out. - Clear, confident communication — you're comfortable picking up the phone and talking a client through an issue. - A willingness to learn new tools and technologies as the role evolves. - Ownership and reliability — you follow through and keep things running smoothly. - Long-term commitment — we're looking to build a lasting working relationship, not fill a short-term gap.

title: WordPress Developer — Elementor
description: Summary We are a US-based digital marketing agency that builds and manages WordPress websites for professional services clients across legal, e-commerce, healthcare, travel, landscaping, retail, and nonprofit. A portfolio is required. Proposals without links to live WordPress sites you have built will not be considered. What Agency Pace Means We want to be direct about this because it is the reason this role exists. In an agency environment, web development moves on client timelines, not open-ended project timelines. Here is what we consider normal throughput for this role: — A full client website (5–10 pages, standard service business) should move from approved wireframe to staging review in 2–3 weeks, not 2–3 months — A single landing page or interior page build should take hours, not days — Page revisions based on feedback should be turned around within 24–48 hours — You should be able to manage 2–3 active projects simultaneously without losing quality or missing deadlines If you are someone who needs weeks to build a single page or frequently misses deadlines, this is not the right fit. If you are fast, organized, and take pride in shipping clean work on schedule, you will do very well here. What You Will Do Website Builds & Page Development — Build complete client websites in WordPress using Elementor Theme Builder from wireframes, mockups, or detailed page briefs provided by the founder — Create and customize page templates, headers, footers, archive pages, single post templates, and dynamic content layouts in Elementor — Build service pages, landing pages, blog layouts, contact pages, about pages, team pages, and other standard business site pages — Implement mobile-responsive design across all breakpoints — every page must look clean on desktop, tablet, and mobile — Build on staging environments and push to production after founder review and approval WordPress Administration & Plugin Management — Install, configure, and troubleshoot WordPress plugins including forms (Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7), SEO (Rank Math), caching, security, and image optimization (Imagify) — Manage WordPress updates (core, theme, plugins) and resolve conflicts or issues that arise from updates — Configure domain connections, SSL, hosting environment settings, and DNS as needed — Set up and maintain staging environments for safe development and testing — Troubleshoot site issues — broken layouts, plugin conflicts, slow load times, form errors, 404s — and resolve them without being asked twice Performance & Quality — Optimize page speed and Core Web Vitals — compress images, minimize CSS/JS, configure caching, and lazy-load media — Ensure cross-browser compatibility (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge) — Implement basic on-page SEO structure as directed (heading hierarchy, alt text, meta fields via Rank Math) — Follow brand guidelines for each client — correct fonts, colors, spacing, and imagery across all pages — QA every page before submitting for review — check links, forms, responsive breakpoints, and load times Collaboration & Process — Work from clear briefs and wireframes provided by the founder — ask clarifying questions early, not after building the wrong thing — Provide time estimates for each build and communicate proactively if timelines shift — Document reusable templates, section libraries, and build patterns so the team can scale — Coordinate with the content and SEO teams when builds require content integration or technical SEO implementation What This Role Is Not — Not a design role — you will receive wireframes, mockups, and brand direction; you are not creating concepts from scratch — Not an SEO strategist, content writer, or marketing role — Not a custom PHP developer or theme coder — we build with Elementor, not custom code (though basic CSS/HTML for adjustments is expected) — Not a general virtual assistant or admin role — Not client-facing — the founder handles all client communication Tools You Will Use You must be highly proficient in WordPress and Elementor. Training provided for agency-specific workflows only. — WordPress (required — this is the entire job) — Elementor Pro / Elementor Theme Builder (required — non-negotiable) — Rank Math (required — for on-page SEO field entry) — Gravity Forms, WPForms, or Contact Form 7 (required) — Imagify or ShortPixel (image optimization) — WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, or equivalent caching plugin — Google PageSpeed Insights / GTmetrix (performance testing) — Canva (basic asset resizing and formatting — not design work) — Google Drive / Docs / Sheets (file and brief management) — Slack (daily communication) — Asana (task management tool familiarity — Asana Preferred) — Staging environments (Bluehost, WP Engine, or equivalent — familiarity required) Must-Haves — Portfolio required — you must include links to live WordPress sites you have built or significantly contributed to. Proposals without a portfolio will not be reviewed. — Minimum 2 years building WordPress websites using Elementor (not just minor edits — full site builds) — Strong proficiency with Elementor Theme Builder including custom headers, footers, archive templates, and dynamic content — Demonstrated ability to build a complete business website (5–10 pages) from wireframe to staging in 2–3 weeks — Experience managing multiple WordPress plugins and resolving plugin conflicts — Mobile-responsive design skills — your sites must look polished on every device — Page speed optimization experience — you know how to get pages loading fast without sacrificing quality — Comfortable working in staging environments and following a staging-to-production deployment workflow — Basic CSS and HTML for fine-tuning layouts, spacing, and responsive adjustments beyond what Elementor handles natively — Experience working across multiple client websites simultaneously without mixing up branding, assets, or instructions — Strong written English — clear communication on timelines, blockers, and questions is essential — Available Monday–Friday with at least 3 hours of overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–12 PM — Reliable internet connection with a backup plan Nice-to-Haves (Not Required, But You Will Stand Out) — Experience building sites for professional services clients (law firms, healthcare, B2B companies) — Familiarity with WooCommerce setup and product page builds — Experience with Elementor custom code widgets or Elementor Pro integrations — Background in an agency environment building sites for multiple clients on rotation — Experience with Google Tag Manager container installation and basic conversion tracking setup — Familiarity with accessibility basics (WCAG compliance, ADA considerations) — Experience with domain migration, site cloning, or hosting transfers — Familiarity with Bluehost or WP Engine hosting environments Hours & Working Style — Starts part-time: 15–30 hours per week, with a clear path to full-time as the client portfolio grows and build volume increases — Long-term engagement — we have a growing pipeline of client sites that need building and ongoing maintenance — Consistent daily availability preferred — web builds move in sprints and require steady progress, not sporadic blocks — At least 3 hours daily overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–12 PM for feedback loops and approvals — You will receive detailed briefs and wireframes — your job is to build fast, build clean, and flag blockers early — You will work alongside the founder (creative direction, client communication, approvals) and coordinate with our content and SEO teams on site launches What We Offer We treat contractors like tea ---------- mbers. After a 90-day evaluation period, you become eligible for the following perks: — Prorated 13th Month Payment — Paid in December or at year-end close, prorated based on months actively engaged after eligibility. — Paid Time Off — 40 hours (5 days) of PTO upon successful completion of the 90-day evaluation period. After one full year of engagement, this increases to 80 hours (10 days) annually. — Sick / Emergency Time — Reasonable notice required. Specific terms defined during onboarding. — Remote Work Allowance — $25 to $50 USD/month to support your internet, power, and workspace costs. Exact amount confirmed in writing based on performance and continued engagement. — Recognized Holidays — Blended Philippine and US holiday calendar agreed upon during onboarding. — Performance Bonus — Discretionary and based on quality, reliability, build speed, and client impact. — Full-Time Conversion — Strong performers during the evaluation period will be offered a transition to full-time hours with expanded responsibilities. 90-Day Evaluation Period: The first 90 days are a mutual evaluation period. During this time, we assess build quality, speed, communication, attention to detail, mobile responsiveness, and ability to manage multiple projects. Contractor perks and full-time consideration begin after successful completion of this period. How to Apply Please start your proposal with the word BUILD so we know you read the full post. In your proposal, please include the following: 1. Links to 2–3 live WordPress sites you built using Elementor. For each, briefly describe your role (full build vs. specific pages), the timeline from start to launch, and any plugins you integrated. A client needs a 7-page professional services website (Home, About, 3 Service pages, Blog, Contact) with a custom header/footer, mobile responsiveness, contact form integration, and basic SEO fields populated. You receive the wireframe and brand assets on day one. How long does it take you to deliver a staging-ready build, and what does your process look like? 3. Are you comfortable working on multiple client sites simultaneously where strategy and creative direction come from the founder, and your focus is building fast and building clean?

Long-term role if all goes well How to apply Start your message with the word "BLUEPRINT" so I know you've actually read this post (you'd be surprised how few do). title: TECHNICAL SUPPORT ENGINEER (AI-ASSISTED TROUBLESHOOTING, INTEGRATIONS, APIs) - US HOURS | G2 AWARD-WINNING US COMPANY
job_title: TECHNICAL SUPPORT ENGINEER (AI-ASSISTED TROUBLESHOOTING, INTEGRATIONS, APIs) - US HOURS | G2 AWARD-WINNING US COMPANY
description: Remote (Philippines) | Full-Time | High-Ownership Career Role | US Hours Required Most support roles are a dead end. This one isn't. You're good at what you do — probably too good for where you are. You troubleshoot issues other people can't figure out. You communicate clearly when things are on fire. You take ownership of problems and drive them to resolution while everyone else is still triaging. And you're stuck. The title doesn't match the work. The growth path is vague. The team doesn't challenge you. The company doesn't see what you're capable of. We do. TOKEN OF TRUST — WHAT WE DO AND WHY IT MATTERS Token of Trust is a G2-recognized, award-winning identity verification platform. Our clients are regulated ecommerce businesses across the US who rely on us to verify real consumers, block fraud, and stay compliant — in industries where getting it wrong means legal exposure, lost revenue, or both. When checkout verification breaks on a customer's live site at 2pm on a Tuesday, we're the team that figures out why and fixes it. We ship weekly. Our last team-wide compensation increase was three months ago. When something breaks, the whole team rallies — not because they have to, but because they care. The engineering team builds the product. The operations team makes sure it works in the real world. This role is the technical backbone of that operations team. THE ROLE We're hiring a Technical Support Engineer to own technical problem-solving across our product and customer integrations. You will: * be the first person to dig into hard technical problems — the ones that require real investigation, not just a script * troubleshoot complex integration issues across WordPress, WooCommerce, Shopify, BigCommerce, and custom platforms * devise and test workarounds for customers, then give the product team clear, actionable information on what's wrong and how to fix it * configure and deploy our product across customer environments — and lead go-lives independently over time * write the playbooks that make recurring issues faster to resolve and easier to delegate * catch product issues before they reach customers through disciplined QA and regression testing * use AI tools daily as a force multiplier — for research, troubleshooting, analysis, and documentation This is not entry-level support. This is not a developer role. This is the kind of role where a strong technical support engineer becomes indispensable — and gets recognized for it. You do not need to write code for this role. Developer experience helps because it gives you intuition for how systems work, but what we need is someone who can configure existing products, read what a system is telling them, and explain it clearly. The ability to understand a system matters more than the ability to build one. WHO THIS IS FOR You're a strong fit if you come from technical support, implementation support, support engineering, QA, or technical operations — and you want a role where your ceiling is set by your performance, not your title. You should be: * the person your team already escalates hard problems to * someone who writes things down so the next person doesn't have to re-investigate * comfortable with structured data, API documentation, and browser dev tools * already using AI tools in your work and seeing the leverage they provide * looking for a team that will challenge you, trust you, and give you room to grow WHAT YOU'LL OWN Technical Support Leadership (Primary Focus) You'll be the senior technical resource on the Operations team — the person who handles issues that require real judgment. * triage, reproduce, and drive resolution of technical support issues * distinguish between user error, configuration issues, integration problems, and product defects * find workarounds for customers while permanent fixes are in progress * gather the right evidence before escalating to Development — so engineers can act immediately, not investigate from scratch * build and improve technical support playbooks so recurring issues can be delegated to the rest of the team * personally drive the hardest, most ambiguous, or most business-critical issues to closure * communicate clearly with customers and internal teams so the right people stay informed without unnecessary noise Where This Role Grows We're a small company, so we promise you will not get bored. Depending upon how quickly you learn, and how broad your interests, you'll be involved in other areas. As you build trust, you'll be invited to expand into spaces where your skills naturally lead, including but not limited to: * **Go-Lives and Integration Enablement** — as the strongest troubleshooter on the ops team, you'll naturally get pulled into the most important and complex client launches. You'll configure plugins and integrations across WordPress, WooCommerce, Shopify, and BigCommerce. You'll join screen-share sessions with customers to resolve setup issues. Over time, you could lead go-lives independently. The core skill is configuring existing systems correctly — not writing new code. * **QA and Release Confidence** — you'll be among the first to test cool new features, find nasty defects, tell development exactly what's wrong, validate fixes before production, and over time help automate regression testing. The goal: we catch issues before customers do. * **Automation and Structured Operations** — you'll use AI with our APIs, logs, and structured data (JSON, YAML, CSV) and source code to investigate and confirm behavior. You'll build lightweight scripts, prompts, checklists, and internal tools that make the whole team faster. You'll help turn recurring patterns into systems so the organization gets stronger every month. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (FIRST 90 DAYS) * you've closed your first complex escalations end-to-end and seen the impact * you've shipped your first playbook and watched someone else use it successfully * technical issues are reproduced faster and escalated with enough context that engineers can act immediately * go-lives become smoother * Development spends less time on preventable support interruptions * leadership gets pulled into fewer emergencies because problems are caught earlier and customers are kept informed REQUIREMENTS * strong written and spoken English * availability to work 8 hours per day within US hours, with US Central overlap required * experience in technical support, Level 2+ support, QA, implementation, or a similar troubleshooting-heavy role * familiarity with ecommerce platforms (WordPress/WooCommerce, Shopify, and/or BigCommerce) * strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills * comfort with structured data (JSON, YAML, CSV), API documentation, and inspecting request/response behavior * ability to write clear bug reports, technical notes, escalation summaries, and playbooks * active daily use of AI/LLM tools (ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) for research, troubleshooting, drafting, and analysis — and the judgment to know when to trust the output vs. verify it yourself * strong follow-through and self-direction * reliable internet and a professional video-call environment PREFERRED * experience using browser dev tools, Postman, curl, or similar debugging tools * basic JavaScript, Python, PHP, or scripting ability — helpful for reading code and understanding systems, not required for the role * experience validating integrations, webhooks, configuration, or data mappings * experience with regression testing or QA process discipline ABOUT THE TRIAL Before a full offer, you'll complete a paid trial project working with one of our real product integrations. The trial tests your ability to install, configure, and work with an existing product — not to write code from scratch. Strong candidates approach it like a support engineer: configure, observe, interpret, and document. Candidates who try to build custom features instead of working with the product as it ships will not pass. COMPENSATION AND GROWTH Starting at $1,100 to $1,500 USD per month depending on experience, hours, and demonstrated technical ability. This will be a combination of incentive-based and hourly pay. Paid trial project before full offer. We are not trying to be the highest-paying listing you'll see today. We are trying to be the best long-term bet for someone who wants to build a career, not just collect a paycheck. This role qualifies for our Growth and Incentive Program. In 2025 alone, tea ---------- mbers received two performance bonuses and four permanent compensation increases. You do not need to find a new job to get a raise here. As we grow, you grow — and we're growing. We reward people who take ownership, raise standards, and deliver consistent results. WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT Most support roles are measured by ticket volume. You close 50 tickets, you're doing great. Nobody asks whether the 51st ticket should have existed in the first place. This role is different. You will be valued for: * solving real problems — not just closing tickets * improving how the company operates * reducing the issues that keep coming back * creating clarity where there was confusion * building systems and playbooks that scale beyond you If you've been waiting for a role where your impact determines your trajectory, this is it. HOW TO APPLY We take hiring seriously because we are protective of our high-performing team and this is a long-term role. It is okay to use AI to help organize or polish your application — in fact, we expect you to. But your answers should reflect your own thinking and experience. Tell us two things: **1. Why this role.** In a few sentences, tell us what caught your attention about this listing and why you think this is the right next step for you. We're not looking for flattery — we want to understand what you're looking for that you're not getting now. **2. The problem you're most proud of solving.** Describe one real technical issue you owned end-to-end. What was the situation, what did you do, and what happened? Keep it to 5-8 sentences. We read every serious application carefully. If this listing described you, we want to hear from you.

title: Full-Stack Engineer
description: If you want to be part of a growing small business that's building with AI and shipping fast, you'll like it here. If you're tired of being one of a hundred engineers maintaining a service you didn't design, this is the opposite. You own the whole stack. You pick your tools. Your work ships in days, not quarters. About: The Mousepad Company is a small US-based DTC brand. We make premium gaming and desk mousepads, printed in-house in California. The team is lean and the owner is hands-on. We ship constantly. The job: You are the owner's technical right hand. Build and maintain our internal app (OPPY) and our customer-facing creator studio (MPCO Studio). You are the only software person on the team. You ship features, integrations, dashboards, and automations: whatever the business needs that week. We do not have a Jira full of cleanly-scoped tickets waiting for you. You help us figure out what to build next. What you do: Phase 1, OPPY (first 30 to 60 days): Take a list of feature requests and ship them. Make the app more efficient, then faster, then more beautiful, in that order. Examples of what we'll ask for: "I click this button and this data shows up." "This page loads in 4 seconds, get it under 1." "This workflow takes 5 clicks, get it to 2." Phase 2, MPCO Studio: Custom mousepad designer web app. Think Figma but exporting creates a print file. More details to be discussed later. Ongoing: Slack custom commands. Notion to Shopify integrations. ---------- to Creator Studio integrations. Financial dashboards. Helping the team use AI better. Internal tools that do not exist yet. When you run out of assigned work, you find what is slow or broken and fix it. Compensation: Monthly salary, paid via Wise. Long-term role. Quarterly performance review with potential raises for top performers. What we need from you: You ship fast and constantly. Your last side project shipped in a weekend, not a year. You live in modern AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, similar) and have opinions on which is best for what. You are a generalist. You can build a Slack bot in the morning, debug a Shopify webhook at lunch, and ship a financial dashboard in the afternoon. You read a stack you have never used and ship in it within a week. You self-direct. Nobody assigns you tickets. You find what matters and do it. Strong written English. Willing to work West Coast US hours. Nice to have: Built something with creator economy or affiliate program tech before. Built a design canvas or image-generation tool before. Shopify, Next.js, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Railway on your résumé. Slack bots, ---------- bots, or Notion integrations on your résumé. A note up front: AI is a tool you live in for this role, so we don't ban it in your application. But generic AI-generated answers are filtered out immediately. Use AI to help you express yourself, not to do the thinking. To apply, send: Ship proof. Link us to something you built recently, alone. Could be a side project, a tool, an integration, anything that ships. Tell us in 3 sentences how long it took and what tools you used to build it. Workflow Loom. Record a 90-second Loom screen-share of your actual coding workflow. Show us your editor, your AI tools, how you move. Don't perform. Just show us what a normal afternoon looks like. Generalist test. Pick one of these three and tell us in plain English how you'd build it. No code, just your approach. (a) A Slack command that pulls last week's blended MER from a PostgreSQL database. (b) A Shopify webhook that auto-creates a Notion task every time a refund over $100 is processed. (c) A creator dashboard showing creator earnings, active design submissions, and approval status.

You will own the client onboarding process after their website is built, ensuring they are fully trained and integrated into our GoHighLevel (GHL) ecosystem. Your goal is to build relationships with clients while designing and maintaining the automation engines that drive their business—from review requests and database reactivation to "voi cemail bombs" and unified communication pipelines. ## What You’ll Do ### Client Onboarding & Account Management Lead the Handoff: Take ownership of the client relationship immediately after the website build is complete. Training & Support: Conduct front-end and back-end training sessions, teaching clients and their teams how to use their new systems (CRM, pipelines, and reporting). Ongoing Communication: Host weekly or monthly performance meetings to review work completed, discuss metrics, and coordinate next steps. Team Liaison: Act as the central point of contact, communicating client needs clearly to the rest of our professional team to ensure nothing falls through the cracks. ### GHL Automation & System Architecture Unified Communications: Set up and maintain a centralized inbox that merges Yelp, website widgets, SMS, and email into one platform. Automated Outreach: Build and manage workflows for automated review requests, referral generation, and repeat appointment reminders. Database Reactivation: Execute "voi cemail bombs" and text/email blasts to send targeted mass communications to leads and customer lists. Phone Systems: Configure VoIP systems for clients, ensuring call tracking, recording, and metrics are functioning correctly. ### Marketing Campaigns & Reporting Lifecycle Marketing: Create and manage email campaigns tailored to specific stages of the sales funnel, including seasonal blasts and monthly newsletters. Chat Widgets: Install and configure website chat widgets for real-time lead capture. Reporting: Design customized dashboards inside GHL that provide clients with clear visibility into their ROI and KPIs. Social & Content: Assist with social media planning for repeat content and ensure consistent messaging across all channels. ### What Success Looks Like (Accountability) Smooth Onboarding: Clients feel confident and supported during the transition from "build" to "live." System Uptime: Automations trigger correctly, and communication channels (VoIP, Chat, SMS) remain active without error. Client Retention: Clients see the value of the software through your regular reporting meetings and proactive support. Documentation: All workflows, client interaction notes, and task statuses are documented clearly in ClickUp. When you apply, write the title of your job post as “GHL Automation Specialist 49 from” and then add your name to be considered. Response Time: Client inquiries regarding their accounts or software are addressed promptly and professionally. ### Your Authority Make decisions on the best automation logic for specific client needs. Propose new GHL features or workflows that could benefit our client base. Manage the client meeting schedule and set the agenda for performance reviews. **Must-Haves (Skills and Tools)** - **Expert-Level GoHighLevel (GHL):** Deep understanding of snapshots, workflows, pipelines, triggers, and smart lists. - **VoIP & Telephony Experience:** Ability to set up Twilio/LeadConnector phone numbers, call forwarding, and voi cemail drops. - **Communication Skills:** Excellent verbal and written English; comfortable leading Zoom calls with business owners and training non-technical staff. - * *Email Marketing:** Experience writing and designing newsletters and drip campaigns that convert. - **Project Management:** Organized in ClickUp or similar PM tools; you document your process and decisions. - **Professional Presence:** Positive, proactive, and solution-focused; camera on during 1:1 and team calls. **Nice-to-Haves** - Experience with N8N or Zapier for integrations outside of GHL. - Basic understanding of SEO and how it feeds into the CRM pipelines. - Experience with social media scheduling tools. - HTML/CSS knowledge for email template customization.

title: Claude Code Expert - Vibe Coder
description: Location: Fully Remote (PH) Schedule: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST (with flexibility as needed for client impact events) About T3 Tech Partners T3 Tech Partners is the team MSPs rely on when challenges exceed Tier 2 or internal expertise. We operate as a Fractional Tier 3 partner, delivering advanced Microsoft 365, cloud, security, and AI engineering expertise to MSPs supporting diverse client environments. We build and operate AI-powered applications that automate the most time-consuming parts of MSP work — tenant management, reporting, security reviews, and migrations. Our stack runs on DigitalOcean and is powered by the Anthropic API. Role Overview We are seeking a senior AI Application Engineer to design, build, and operate production applications powered by the Anthropic API. You'll own the backend services, integrations, and infrastructure that turn Claude into reliable, multi-tenant tooling for MSPs and their clients. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll write the code, ship the features, deploy the services, watch the dashboards, and tune the prompts. You should be equally comfortable architecting a tool-use loop against the Messages API, debugging a Node service on a DigitalOcean droplet, designing a Postgres schema for multi-tenant isolation, and explaining cost trade-offs to leadership. Key Responsibilities Anthropic API & AI Application Development (Core Focus) Design and build production applications on top of the Anthropic API — Messages, tool use, streaming, prompt caching, batch processing, the Files API, and MCP connectors where appropriate. Architect multi-turn agentic workflows, tool-use loops, and structured-output pipelines that hold up against real customer data, not just demos. Implement robust prompt and context engineering practices: system prompt design, dynamic context assembly, retrieval, and output validation. Build evals and regression suites so prompt and model changes don't silently degrade behavior in production. Optimize for cost and latency at scale: prompt caching strategies, model selection (Haiku vs. Sonnet vs. Opus), batch processing for non-realtime workloads, and token budgets per tenant. Implement guardrails: input validation, output verification, rate limiting, abuse detection, and safe handling of customer data. Backend & API Engineering Build and maintain backend services in Python and/or Node.js/TypeScript, exposing clean REST or RPC APIs to internal tools, partner integrations, and end-user products. Design multi-tenant data models in PostgreSQL with proper tenant isolation, encryption, and audit logging. Integrate with the Microsoft Graph, Google Workspace Admin SDK, and MSP platform APIs (SuperOps, Hudu, and similar) to feed Claude with the right context and act on its outputs. Implement authentication and authorization (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, app registrations, service principals) across Microsoft and Google identity ecosystems. Design background job systems, queues, and webhook handlers for long-running AI workflows. DigitalOcean Infrastructure & Operations Own the deployment, scaling, and operations of our application stack on DigitalOcean — Droplets, App Platform, Managed Databases (Postgres, Redis), Spaces, VPCs, and load balancers. Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar) for automated testing, deployment, and rollback. Containerize services with Docker; manage configuration, secrets, and environment promotion across dev/staging/prod. Implement observability: structured logging, metrics, request tracing, and AI-specific telemetry (token usage, latency, eval scores, cost per tenant). Maintain backup, disaster recovery, and security baselines for production workloads. Harden services for the realities of running customer-data-handling apps: TLS, secret rotation, dependency hygiene, and least-privilege IAM. Integration with MSP & Microsoft 365 Workflows Build integrations against the Microsoft Graph and Google Workspace Admin SDK to power AI features over real tenant data — mailboxes, drives, identities, devices, and policies. Develop and maintain PowerShell components where Microsoft tooling demands it, and bridge cleanly back to the main backend. Support T3's product work (including T3nant Wiz) and internal MSP delivery tooling with shared services and libraries. Work with the rest of the team to identify high-leverage automation opportunities and ship them. Engineering Discipline Write clean, tested, reviewed code. Treat AI-generated code as a draft to be read, not output to be trusted. Maintain meaningful test coverage — unit, integration, and AI-output evals. Participate in code review, design discussions, and post-i ---------- reviews. Document architecture, runbooks, and operational procedures so the team can support what you build. Availability & Support Expectations Standard working hours are 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST. Some flexibility is required for production deployments, i ---------- response, or critical client work outside normal hours. This role is not on-call, but responsiveness during critical events is expected. Qualifications Required Experience 5+ years of hands-on backend or full-stack engineering experience shipping production applications. Demonstrable production experience building applications on the Anthropic API or directly comparable LLM APIs (OpenAI, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock). You should be able to walk us through real systems you've built — tool-use loops, streaming UIs, evals, cost optimizations, and the trade-offs behind each. Strong Python or Node.js/TypeScript for backend service development. Solid PostgreSQL experience: schema design, query tuning, migrations, multi-tenant patterns. Production experience deploying and operating services on DigitalOcean (or directly comparable IaaS — AWS, Azure, GCP, Linode, Hetzner). Strong Linux, shell, and command-line fluency. Solid Git and modern software engineering hygiene (PRs, code review, CI/CD, testing). Working knowledge of HTTP, REST, OAuth 2.0, and webhook patterns. Excellent native-level English communication skills, both written and verbal. Strongly Preferred Hands-on experience with prompt caching, batch API, tool use, and the Files API in production. Experience building or evaluating AI evals in production environments. Experience with the Microsoft Graph and/or Google Workspace Admin SDK. PowerShell proficiency for Microsoft 365 administration. Experience with Docker, GitHub Actions, and modern deployment tooling. Familiarity with MSP platforms (SuperOps, Hudu, ConnectWise, Datto, or similar). Prior experience handling customer data under compliance frameworks (CMMC, HIPAA, SOC 2). A public GitHub presence or portfolio of AI applications you can share. How You Work You read AI output critically. You don't ship code you haven't understood. You think about cost, latency, and failure modes from day one — not as an afterthought. You're comfortable saying "this shouldn't be AI" when that's the right call. You can drop into an unfamiliar codebase or API and get useful work done without hand-holding. A few notes: I left in the M365/Graph integration emphasis because that's clearly where T3's domain value is — pull it back if this person is mostly building T3nant Wiz product features and you want a different hire for MSP delivery tooling. "AI Application Engineer" is the cleanest title for SEO and candidate filtering. "Senior AI Engineer" or "Senior Backend Engineer (AI)" also work. The DigitalOcean line in "Strongly Preferred — comparable IaaS" is intentional. Restricting to DO-only experience will shrink your candidate pool meaningfully and DO is easy to ramp on if someone knows AWS or Azure. I want someone to talk to you like I do in Claude code and produce apps like I do without the need for full stack development7:08 AMClaude responded: Ah, that's a meaningfully different role.Ah, that's a meaningfully different role. You want someone who's a skilled Claude Code operator — strong taste, strong judgment, strong communication with the model — not someone who's going to hand-roll a React frontend or argue about ORM choices. Location: Fully Remote (PH) Schedule: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST (with flexibility as needed for client impact events) About T3 Tech Partners T3 Tech Partners is the team MSPs rely on when challenges exceed Tier 2 or internal expertise. We operate as a Fractional Tier 3 partner, delivering advanced Microsoft 365, cloud, security, and AI engineering expertise to MSPs supporting diverse client environments. We build and ship AI-powered applications fast — using Claude Code as our primary engineering tool. Our stack runs on DigitalOcean and is powered by the Anthropic API. Role Overview We are seeking a Claude Code Builder to ship production applications by working with Claude Code, not around it. This is not a traditional full-stack developer role. We are not looking for someone who wants to handcraft React components, debate framework choices, or write every line themselves. We are looking for someone who can sit down with Claude Code, describe what needs to be built clearly and precisely, review what it produces with a sharp eye, course-correct it when it goes sideways, and ship working applications to production. The skill we're hiring for is directing an AI engineer effectively — knowing what to ask for, what to push back on, when to start over, when to dig into the code yourself, and when to trust the agent. If your instinct on reading this is "that's not real engineering," this isn't the role for you. If your instinct is "finally, someone gets it" — keep reading. What You'll Actually Do Build apps with Claude Code as your primary tool. You'll spend most of your day in a Claude Code session, describing features, reviewing diffs, running tests, deploying to DigitalOcean, and iterating. You'll ship more in a week than a traditional dev ships in a month — because you know how to drive the agent. Translate fuzzy MSP problems into clear specs. A partner says "we need something that audits Conditional Access policies across all our tenants." You turn that into a working app — by talking it through with Claude Code, not by sitting down to architect it yourself first. Review AI-generated code with judgment. You read every diff. You catch hallucinated APIs, weak error handling, security holes, and subtle logic bugs. You know when "looks fine" is fine and when it isn't. Operate production apps on DigitalOcean. Deploys, logs, fixing things when they break. You don't need to be a sysadmin — you need to be able to ask Claude Code to set up a Droplet, review what it did, and notice when it's wrong. Wire up integrations. Microsoft Graph, Google Workspace Admin SDK, MSP tools (SuperOps, Hudu) — Claude Code knows how to call these APIs; your job is making sure the result actually solves the problem. Build evals and guardrails. Make sure the AI features in your apps don't silently degrade. Catch regressions before clients do. Ship. Working software in production, used by real people, on a regular cadence. How You Work This is the most important section. Read it carefully. You think in prompts and plans, not classes and interfaces. When you see a problem, your first move is to talk it through clearly — not to open an IDE and start typing. You have strong taste. You can look at a UI and say "this is ugly, do it again." You can read code and say "this is fragile, refactor it." Taste is the thing that separates good Claude Code operators from people who ship slop. You read every line. You don't merge what you haven't understood. If you can't explain what a piece of code does, you ask Claude Code to explain it, or you simplify it until you can. You know when to stop the agent. When Claude Code is going in circles, you don't let it burn through tokens — you stop, reset context, and try a different approach. You write good CLAUDE.md files, plans, and specs. You understand that the quality of the output is mostly a function of the quality of the context you provide. You don't romanticize hand-coding. You also don't worship the agent. You use the right tool for the job, and most of the time the right tool is Claude Code with a clear spec and a careful reviewer. You can debug. When something breaks, you can drop into the code, read it, and figure out what's wrong — even if you didn't write it. You don't need to write idiomatic React fro ---------- mory, but you need to be able to read it. What This Role Is Not Not a full-stack developer role. We don't need someone whose identity is "I write code." Not a prompt engineer role. We're not paying you to tweak system prompts in a vacuum. Not a no-code role. Claude Code produces real code, in real repos, with real tests. You need to be technical enough to review it and operate it. Not a research role. We ship apps that solve MSP problems. Today. Availability & Support Expectations Standard working hours are 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST. Some flexibility is required for production deployments or critical client work outside normal hours. This role is not on-call, but responsiveness during critical events is expected. Qualifications Required Demonstrable, daily, production-level use of Claude Code (or directly comparable agentic coding tools — Cursor agent mode, Aider, etc.). You should be able to share a screen and walk us through a real session: how you set up context, how you review output, how you recover when things go wrong. This is the single most important qualification. A portfolio of shipped applications built primarily with AI-assisted coding. GitHub repos, deployed apps, internal tools — something we can look at. Be honest about what was AI-generated vs. hand-written; we're not impressed by people pretending they wrote it all themselves. Enough technical fluency to review code in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript. You don't need to write it from scratch fluently. You do need to read it, understand it, and catch obvious problems. Working comfort with the command line, Git, and basic Linux. You can SSH into a Droplet, read logs, run commands. You can manage branches, write commits, open PRs. Working knowledge of HTTP, REST APIs, JSON, and basic database concepts. Not deep expertise — enough to direct Claude Code intelligently and spot when it's doing something dumb. Experience deploying and operating apps on DigitalOcean (or directly comparable — Vercel, Railway, ---------- , Render, AWS, Azure). Again, you don't need to be a sysadmin — you need to have shipped real things to real environments and dealt with the consequences. Strong written communication. Most of your job is writing — to Claude Code, to your teammates, to MSP partners. If you can't write clearly, you can't direct an AI agent effectively. Excellent native-level English, both written and verbal. Strongly Preferred Familiarity with the Anthropic API directly — Messages, tool use, prompt caching. Experience with the Microsoft Graph or Google Workspace Admin SDK. PowerShell familiarity for M365 administration. Familiarity with MSP platforms (SuperOps, Hudu, ConnectWise, Datto). A public presence — blog posts, GitHub, X threads, YouTube — where you've shared how you work with AI tools. What We Don't Care About Computer science degree. Years of "traditional" full-stack experience. Whether you can implement a linked list on a whiteboard. Framework preferences. The agent has them; you don't need to. How to Apply Send us: A 5–10 minute screen recording of you using Claude Code to build or modify something real. Don't polish it. We want to see how you actually work — including the parts where you reset and try again. Links to 1–3 things you've shipped with AI-assisted coding, with a short note on what you built and what role the AI played. A short paragraph on a time Claude Code (or a similar tool) was wrong, and how you caught it. No cover letter. No resume formatting Olympics. Show us how you work.
